matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue in Theorem 3.3: the ground truth notes the loss is expressed without the softmax normalization term, while the finding observes a contradiction between the main text (which includes -log∑e^{z_j}) and the appendix (which omits it). Both point to an incomplete/incorrect formulation of the LS loss at the same location.

The ground truth concerns asymmetric hyperparameter tuning between MaxSup and competing methods under altered training protocols. The findings do not address this experimental design fairness issue; no finding discusses unequal optimization effort or hyperparameter tuning disparities.

The ground truth identifies unusually large within-class distance values for Logit Penalty in Table 2 that contradict existing literature. The findings do not mention Table 2, Logit Penalty metrics, or any data integrity issues related to intra-class variation statistics.

The ground truth critiques the causal claim in Section 1 that the error amplification term 'exacerbates representation collapse' as oversimplified and insufficiently supported. The findings do not address this specific causal attribution claim in the Introduction.

Both identify the same issue in Table 7 (long-tailed CIFAR-10): the ground truth notes the paper fails to acknowledge/analyze zero accuracy for low-shot classes, while the finding reports exactly 0.0 accuracy for minority classes across all methods as implausible. Both point to the same ethical/transparency concern about ignoring limitations in imbalanced settings.

The ground truth identifies suspiciously uniform and small standard deviations in Tables 4 and 5 as a data integrity issue. The findings do not mention standard deviation patterns, variance reporting, or any statistical anomalies in these tables.

The ground truth identifies an error in Section 3.2's gradient derivation (Equation 9) that neglects the shared dependency on mean logit. The findings do not address gradient analysis or Equation 9; finding 5 discusses a different inconsistency in Table 1's error amplification formulation.

Both identify overclaiming in conclusions. The ground truth notes Section 5 claims 'superior transfer performance' broadly despite experimental limitations. Finding 4 identifies an unsupported quantitative claim in Section 4.4 about Grad-CAM metrics. Both point to claim distortion where assertions exceed supporting evidence, though at different specific locations.

Both identify citation issues. The ground truth notes reference [11] (Heinonen et al. 2025) is fabricated/untraceable for CIFAR-10-C settings. Finding 2 identifies a misattribution where reference [3] points to an unrelated paper. While the specific citations differ, both detect reference integrity problems undermining experimental credibility.

The ground truth identifies an inconsistency where Section 4.2.1 states CutMix/Mixup are disabled for DeiT-Small, but Appendices G and J describe models trained with them enabled. The findings do not address this experimental setup contradiction regarding data augmentation.

The ground truth critiques the abstract's promotional rhetoric claiming MaxSup is 'a more robust alternative' without qualification. The findings do not address abstract language, rhetorical tone, or presentation manipulation issues.
